title: The Cold Drop
premise: Ada Fairweather, a financial-crimes investigator who secretly launders intelligence funds for a shadowy handler network, receives a meeting invite from her dead handler, Marcus Vane. Following it, she discovers Vane faked his death to expose 'the Cold Drop' — a slush fund that lets the powerful buy impunity — and left her the ledger as both weapon and target. Hunted by the fund's enforcer and betrayed by her own agency's director, Ada must choose between trading the ledger for her own survival or burning it to expose everyone, including herself. In the end she releases the ledger publicly, accepts arrest on her own terms, and finds that the lover she lied to chooses to stand beside her in the fallout.
about_author: Rafael Montrose is the pen name of a former compliance officer who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people who discover the systems they serve were never meant to be clean.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She closes another spotless case at the Financial Conduct Authority while hiding her double life laundering for an off-books intelligence unit. Her go-bag sits by the door; her boyfriend Daniel believes every polished lie. Beat: controlled dread beneath competence.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. An encrypted calendar invite arrives from Marcus Vane — dead nine days by official record — scheduling a meeting for tomorrow, 6 p.m., at a hotel bar. She verifies the cryptographic signature: authentic. Beat: vertigo; the ground tilts.

chapters.title: Six O'Clock
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the bar she watches a stranger take Vane's usual seat: a woman named Ilse Brandt who claims Vane is alive and needs Ada to move one last payment. Ada notices surveillance in the mirrors. Beat: suspicion sharpening into fear.

chapters.title: Vane's Ghost
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Flashback structure reveals Ilse was Vane's fixer; he staged his death after finding the Cold Drop ledger, leaving instructions to recruit Ada. Ilse omits that she's already been paid twice to find him first. Beat: divided loyalty.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A courier delivers a burner phone with a single photo: page one of the Cold Drop ledger, listing names she knows — judges, ministers, her own director. The price of silence is her continued laundering; the price of exposure is everything. Beat: temptation and terror.

chapters.title: Director Hale
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Ada's boss quietly requests her personnel file and flags her travel patterns, revealing he suspects her double life — and is himself on the ledger. He assigns her a friendly 'protection detail.' Beat: the cage closing politely.

chapters.title: Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She tells Daniel a half-truth about a work crisis, packs the bag, and tests the burner. Vane's voice message gives coordinates and a warning: trust no one from the old network, especially Ilse. Beat: love fraying under duty.

chapters.title: Amsterdam
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She flies under a false name and meets Vane in a canal-side safehouse. He shows her the full ledger and his plan: release it through three independent journalists simultaneously so it can't be buried. He asks her to be the fourth channel. Beat: conviction is contagious.

chapters.title: What Ada Knows
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. He admits he chose Ada not for skill but because her laundering records are in the ledger too — she has skin in the game, making her incorruptible by ordinary means. Ada feels used and, worse, understood. Beat: betrayal braided with intimacy.

chapters.title: The Enforcer
chapters.summary: Kovac's POV. The Cold Drop's enforcer traces the Amsterdam flight and reports to Director Hale, who realizes Vane lives. Kovac is authorized to make the problem disappear — permanently. Beat: cold professional menace.

chapters.title: Safehouse Burned
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Kovac hits the safehouse early; Vane covers Ada's escape through the canals but is captured. Ada escapes with a partial copy of the ledger and a dead journalist's contact card. Beat: guilt, adrenaline, grief deferred.

chapters.title: Daniel
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Agents visit Daniel with photos of Ada and questions about her finances. He defends her instinctively, then searches their flat and finds the go-bag, the second phone, the lies. Beat: heartbreak as discovery.

chapters.title: Bargaining Chips
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale offers Ada immunity in exchange for the ledger and Vane's location, dangling Daniel's safety. Ada pretends to consider while realizing Hale's offer proves how much the list frightens him. Beat: playing powerless while holding power.

chapters.title: Ilse Returns
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse intercepts Ada, confesses she sold Vane out once and offers to help free him as penance — she knows the black-site facility where he's held. Ada must decide whether a traitor can be trusted twice. Beat: uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada offers Hale the ledger's physical copy — a decoy — in exchange for access to the facility where 'a witness' is held. Hale takes the bait because destroying evidence matters more than procedure. Beat: the con within the con.

chapters.title: Black Site
chapters.summary: Ada and Ilse's alternating POV. Inside the facility they find Vane drugged but alive; extraction goes wrong when Kovac anticipates them. Ilse takes a bullet buying time. Beat: sacrifice, chaos, no clean exits.

chapters.title: Interrogation Room
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Captured again, Vane faces Hale across a table — two men who built the machine arguing over who broke it first. Vane stalls, revealing he seeded the ledger with a dead-man's-switch release. Beat: moral rot laid bare.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Switch
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Hiding in the city, Ada triggers the switch: the full ledger, unredacted including her own name, goes to forty journalists worldwide. There is no undoing it, no deal now. Beat: point of no return, strangely calm.

chapters.title: Kovac's Last Contract
chapters.summary: Kovac's POV. Ordered to kill Ada before the story lands, Kovac instead reads the ledger, finds his own handlers listed, and walks away — mailing his files to a newspaper first. Beat: the instrument refusing the hand.

chapters.title: Exposure
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The story detonates: resignations, arrests, Hale burning documents then fleeing, Vane surrendering publicly to control the narrative. Ada watches from a crowded pub as her own name scrolls past strangers who barely react. Beat: catharsis laced with anticlimax.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada turns herself in, giving a full statement including her crimes. Daniel visits the interview room; she expects nothing and offers him the truth without varnish. He doesn't forgive her yet — but he stays. Beat: love chosen against duty's wreckage.

chapters.title: The Cold Drop Dries Up
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, months later. Disgraced but useful, Ada consults for the inquiry from a prison work-release program; some names escaped, but the fund is dead. On a grey morning she unpacks the go-bag at last and puts it in storage. Beat: hard-won, imperfect peace.
